title: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist in Finland – Room by Room
description: Move-out cleaning checklist for kitchens, bathrooms, floors, cupboards and final checks before returning your keys.
lead: Plan your move-out clean after your belongings have been removed. First review the terms of your tenancy or property handover, which may require specific cleaning tasks.

sections.p: Empty the rooms and any storage space. Make sure the cleaner can access the property and has enough time before handover.
bullets: Confirm when the keys must be returned.
Get a written list of tasks included in the cleaning quote.
Agree separately on windows and balconies if needed.

sections.p: Grease and food residue build up in kitchens. Check whether appliance interiors and cupboards are included.
bullets: Wipe worktops, cupboard doors and shelves.
Clean the hob and agreed oven surfaces.
Clean the fridge and freezer as agreed.
Check the sink, taps, waste cupboard and floor.

sections.p: Limescale and drains may require additional work, so discuss them in advance.
bullets: Clean sinks, taps and the toilet.
Wash the agreed floor and wall surfaces.
Check mirrors and shelves.
Confirm whether the floor drain and sauna are included.

sections.p: Inspect the property in daylight after cleaning and document its condition.
bullets: Wipe cupboards and fixtures included in your agreement.
Vacuum and mop with appropriate care for the floor material.
Check doors, switches and visible skirting boards.
Photograph rooms and report any issues promptly.

title: Home Cleaning Prices – How to Compare Quotes in Finland
description: Understand Finnish home cleaning prices: hourly charges, minimum bookings, supplies, travel, additional work and VAT.
h1: Home cleaning prices and quote comparison
lead: Compare the total cost of home cleaning rather than looking only at the advertised hourly rate. Tasks, estimated time and charging methods can differ.

sections.p: The price can depend on floor area, complexity, location, timing and how often the cleaning is carried out.
bullets: Ask for the total price or hourly price including applicable VAT.
Check any minimum number of hours.
Ask whether travel, equipment and products are included.
Confirm separate charges for oven cleaning, windows and other extras.

sections.p: A quote that includes equipment and travel is not directly comparable with one that charges for them separately. Provide the same description and expected duration to every provider.

sections.h: Agree on the work in writing
sections.p: Confirm the scope, date, price and change or cancellation terms. Ask what happens if the work takes longer than expected.

title: Household Tax Deduction for Cleaning in Finland
description: Could your cleaning service qualify for a Finnish household tax deduction? Learn what to check and find official guidance from Vero.
lead: Cleaning work carried out at your home may be eligible for the Finnish household tax deduction (kotitalousvähennys), depending on current rules and the provider.

sections.h: Check the work and provider's eligibility
sections.p: Consult the Finnish Tax Administration's current rules to determine whether the work is deductible and which requirements apply to the provider. One factor to check is registration in the prepayment register.
Keep invoices and proof of payment. Separating labour costs from other charges can affect the amount eligible for deduction.
The deduction rate, threshold and maximum can change. Check the rules for the relevant tax year before making a decision.
bullets: Official guidance: https://www.vero.fi/en/individuals/tax-cards-and-tax-returns/income-and-deductions/household-expenses/
Keep the provider's business ID and itemised invoice.
Check the eligibility of the exact work and payment year.
